assessment_kind: Structural design/constraint evaluation, not raster or runtime test

candidate_definitions.A: Collar forward of pelvis 3–4 px at rest; pelvis-to-rib axis about 14°. Preserve a shallow connected curve, not a permanently falling line.
candidate_definitions.B: Collar forward of pelvis about 3 px; pelvis-to-rib axis about 9.5°. Short waist connection and a mobile curve; rest is not deep crouch.

candidate_definitions.A: Void center +4 px ahead of pelvis in idle, +12 run, +18 dash, +17 contact. Anatomical neck remains attached.
candidate_definitions.B: Void center +3 px idle, +6 run, +12 dash, +9 contact. Attached neck; no head-led impact surface.

candidate_definitions.A: Right/grip shoulder 1 px nearer the neck than left in baseline; chest-forward excursion dominates this small offset.
candidate_definitions.B: Right/grip shoulder is about 2 px higher than left in upright enclosed targets; carry its collar-side anatomical role with the torso through oblique keys, not an exact screen-y gap.

candidate_definitions.A: Rib center leads pelvis by 3 px idle, 8 run, 10 dash/contact; approximately 14–45° forward axis in six targets.
candidate_definitions.B: Rib center leads pelvis by 2 px idle, 3 run, 5 dash, 0 antic, 6 contact, 2 recovery; approximately 0–25° forward axis.

candidate_definitions.A: Near-level belt plane, projecting after the chest. Use 1–2 px belt tilt with alternating contact; no rotating rigid cutout.
candidate_definitions.B: Near-level belt plane initiates the support transfer; 1–2 px tilt alternates with support. Ribcage yaw/lean responds at smaller or later amplitude.

candidate_definitions.A: Torso/pelvis drawing proxy moves toward front support; an excursion needs subsequent retrieval. Never equate this proxy with measured whole-body mass.
candidate_definitions.B: Proxy stays within static support in quiet keys, moves forward in action and is recontained. A running mass need not be within the current foot at every instant.

candidate_definitions.A: Right leg favored at rest; both anatomical legs alternate without a permanent weaker side. A forward catch is not a forced gameplay step.
candidate_definitions.B: Right leg favored at rest; both legs alternate. A support/down accent precedes chest opening. Equal competent legs; no permanent unilateral drag.

candidate_definitions.A: Wide action/grip versus trailing free arm; six targets have 22–33 px horizontal wrist separation. One narrow free-elbow window remains required.
candidate_definitions.B: Right grip stays below head/face, left elbow supplies a 2–3 px open wedge against ribs; six targets have 20–29 px wrist separation. No paired raised fists.

candidate_definitions.A: Distinct right contact/down, passing/flight, left contact/down and return, with faster visual gathering under advancing chest.
candidate_definitions.B: The same complete bilateral support sequence; loading accents precede short chest releases. Alternate legs fully rather than mirroring half a gait.

candidate_definitions.A: Upper chest visually commits first; pelvis and support catch the advance.
candidate_definitions.B: Support loading and pelvis drive lead the action; ribcage initially stays enclosed beneath the right shoulder.

candidate_definitions.A: Pelvis/support retrieval then trailing shoulder, free wrist and attached flame. This chain may need more than the remaining visible exposure.
candidate_definitions.B: Chest opens after support drive; left wrist and flame finish after torso reclosure. Offsets are spatial/pose relationships within the current clock, never extra input delay.

candidate_definitions.A: Actual root accelerates immediately; chest lead grows 3→8 px rib-to-pelvis across selected keys, then support catches. No planted prelaunch hold.
candidate_definitions.B: Actual root accelerates immediately; pelvis changes first in the pose, rib lead grows 2→3 px and chest briefly opens. No brace wait.

candidate_definitions.A: Actual friction/reversal changes root velocity; chest retains forward excursion until a support retrieval key. Cancellation may omit that defining catch.
candidate_definitions.B: Real braking loads support; rib lead shrinks toward 0–2 px while the left elbow stays legible. No forced skid duration or additional displacement.

candidate_definitions.A: Compact chest commitment, retaining consistent right striker; six-target antic rib lead 3 px. Returning from run to this key drops rib lead by 5 px.
candidate_definitions.B: Rib center nearly above pelvis, grip below face, right shoulder close to collar; antic rib lead 0 px. From run the lead changes only 3 px.

candidate_definitions.A: Right palm/weapon acts forward with pelvis trailing chest by 10 px; head lead 17 px. Support and restoration must justify the overreach.
candidate_definitions.B: Pelvis projects, chest opens to 6 px lead, right hand connects forward while left elbow stays separate; head lead 9 px. No trained straight-punch guard.

candidate_definitions.A: Support/pelvis retrieves the chest before wrist/secondary settling. The law is clearest only if the catch is displayed.
candidate_definitions.B: Rib lead contracts to 2 px and protective shoulder relation remains; wrist/secondary settle afterwards. A cut can discard final settle without changing the body's identity.

candidate_definitions.A: Discard unfinished catch on real cancel; use destination pose and preserve anatomical ownership. A frozen/cut lunge risks leaving only stock reach.
candidate_definitions.B: Discard final settle on real cancel; choose the destination compact/open key directly, retaining protected shoulder, support relationship and grip. No mandatory rest reset.

candidate_definitions.A: Use facing × (texture point − pivot); anatomical right remains right and leg phase is not swapped. Large head lead reverses instantly with facing even while velocity still opposes it.
candidate_definitions.B: Same transform/ownership. Smaller lead permits a compact braking pose when facing changes before velocity crosses zero; no interpolated turn-through-front.

candidate_definitions.A: Rest grip (48,32) matches legacy offset. Target grip travel reaches local (27,-29); fixed legacy anchor cannot hold the arm through action.
candidate_definitions.B: Rest grip (48,32) matches legacy offset. Target contact (56,32), local (24,-30), requires pose metadata; no change to prop state, collision, reach or transformation time.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Eligible buffered swing starts at actual _atk_t=0; +60 horizontal step. Run distance continues underneath grounded attack.
interrupt_checks.A: Run rib lead 8→antic 3 px, head lead 12→4 px. Without a bridge this cuts away the defining catch; an inserted bridge would consume startup. Destination must still be chosen directly.
interrupt_checks.B: Run rib lead 3→antic 0 px, head lead 6→2 px. Compact load can replace running without a rest reset or new timer; keep right grip and current support.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Allowed only with dash remaining ≤60 ms; move state becomes NORMAL, dash momentum retained. Startup time still exists but picker skips a0 to a1.
interrupt_checks.A: Dash head lead 18→contact 17 px leaves only a long lunge until a catch is shown. Candidate identity risks disappearing when later recovery is canceled.
interrupt_checks.B: Dash head lead 12→contact 9 px and enclosed right shoulder remain. Direct contact/commit key carries inherited momentum; no backward reload.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Dash blocked through startup/active (_atk_t≤170 ms); allowed during recovery if cooldown/buffer/air-dash gates permit. _end_swing occurs on cancel.
interrupt_checks.A: A visible catch is not guaranteed before dash; early eligible cancellation can erase the defining retrieval. Never wait for it or change the buffer.
interrupt_checks.B: Drop pending settle and select dash entry immediately. Enclosure and right ownership persist; no obligatory recovery/idle drawing.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: No dedicated gameplay landing lock. Buffered attack checks current eligibility; floor state is sampled before move_and_slide, so presentation may change on the next physics/visual update.
interrupt_checks.A: Required catch may conflict with immediate loaded strike; do not force a planted corrective step or land hold.
interrupt_checks.B: Existing support load supplies preparation; attack can replace cosmetic landing at once. Do not claim a newly authored landing frame exists in today's picker.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Freeze 280 ms preserves cooldown/buffers; gravity/movement continue and visuals are skipped. Arrival opens eligibility, not a guarantee that a cooling attack fires immediately.
interrupt_checks.A: Held reach may return directly to a new action without a catch. Body identity then depends mostly on a static lean.
interrupt_checks.B: Resume selected destination at the actual clock when eligible; compact shoulder/grip remain identifiable without completing arrival settle. If cooldown persists, do not show fake active contact.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: set_fight_frozen(true) ends current swing. Last selected drawing is held because visuals are skipped; root keeps moving under gravity. It is not an attack paused for continuation.
interrupt_checks.A: A reached key can remain frozen without support retrieval; no invisible catch may be imagined. Select real postfreeze state directly.
interrupt_checks.B: Hold exact drawing and its anchor through freeze, with no new secondary advance; clear the pending swing picture on normal visual reentry. No replay of old recovery or contact.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Accepted nonfatal damage sets _hurt_t=120 ms and knockback; it does not cancel the attack. Attack picker has priority, so standalone hurt can be entirely hidden by the remaining swing.
interrupt_checks.A: Use only a same-phase strain variant if later visual integration supports it; do not force a separate catch/flinch sequence or reverse contact direction.
interrupt_checks.B: A short added contraction/left-elbow disruption can preserve the right striker and existing attack phase. This is a future presentation variant, not a current selector feature or a gameplay cancel.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Attack presentation keeps priority until attack ends; remaining hurt time can show afterward. Dash may also outrank hurt. No new hurt lock.
interrupt_checks.A: Do not try to complete retrieval before the real destination. A lost catch and residual off-balance pose can be confused with another attack.
interrupt_checks.B: Select appropriate same-phase strain/residual hurt without a new wait; return or cancel keeps the same support/grip relationships. Fatal hit follows separate died path.

interrupt_checks.current_gameplay: Facing changes immediately from input while velocity is still old-direction; reverse acceleration and _skid already exist, run distance does not reset.
interrupt_checks.A: A long lead flips before travel reverses; must author compact braking. This reduces the very feature that otherwise defines A.
interrupt_checks.B: Use compact loaded key with 0–2 px rib lead; old-travel flame lag may remain briefly attached. Keep current leg phase and anatomical hand, not a swapped half-cycle.

anti_generic_checks.A: Idle inclination and unresolved run-end lean can collapse to a stock slouch.

final_law_sentence: The support leg drives the pelvis while the ribcage stays enclosed beneath the neckward right shoulder, opens briefly for the action, and returns over support before the arms and attached flame settle.

final_invariants.name: Registered physical construction
final_invariants.rule: Every BODY/FLAME frame keeps the 64×64 native canvas, pivot (32,62), connected anatomy and the same material volumes; projection/occlusion and articulated bending replace scaling or changing limb length. A separate weapon module keeps its own registered hilt pivot.

final_invariants.name: Persistent upper-body ownership
final_invariants.rule: The anatomical right shoulder is the collar-side shoulder (about 2 px higher than the left in upright enclosed keys), and the left elbow owns the open rib-side wedge; contact may release enclosure but never swaps these anatomical roles. Carry this relationship in torso-local construction through oblique poses and collapse, not as a fixed screen-up offset.

final_invariants.name: One grip/striker
final_invariants.rule: The anatomical right hand is the grip and primary contact hand in every frame and facing; its connected shoulder/elbow/wrist chain and pose anchor persist even when occluded or the weapon is broken. The left hand never silently becomes the grip.

final_invariants.name: Support-led causal rhythm
final_invariants.rule: Voluntary exertion starts from support/pelvis drive and a protected torso, with brief opening and support retrieval where time survives; interruption selects the real destination without an obligatory completion. Airborne release and fatal support failure are consequences of that chain, not invented grounded steps.

final_invariants.name: Body before attached self-image
final_invariants.rule: BODY alone must retain the person and action; FLAME is faceless secondary anatomy rooted at the same neck, obeys the selected/frozen presentation and never supplies damage, an independent projectile, glow or a substitute for physical body mass.

drawable_delay_rule: Drawable overlap target: when a return is actually displayed, put the rib center back within its +1–3 px recovery relation while the left wrist is still 1–2 px short of its final settle position and the flame tips still trail the prior opening. Resolve them in at most the next available authored exposure. During run, place the pelvis at its loading/contact relation before the key that opens the ribs. This is redrawn pose spacing, not a separately simulated limb or an added millisecond delay; if the enclosing state is replaced or too short, omit the delayed settle.
